# ADA.gov

> > Official U.S. Department of Justice resource for the Americans with Disabilities Act, providing regulations, compliance guidance, and enforcement information for disability civil rights.

ADA.gov is maintained by the DOJ Civil Rights Division and serves as the authoritative source for ADA Title II (state/local government) and Title III (public accommodations) requirements. The site includes full statutory text, implementing regulations, technical assistance manuals, and guidance on topics ranging from web accessibility to service animals.

## Key Topics

- Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
- Title II - State and Local Government
- Title III - Public Accommodations
- Department of Justice Civil Rights Division
- ADA Standards for Accessible Design
- Web and Mobile Accessibility (WCAG)
- Service Animals
- Disability Rights and Anti-Discrimination
- Effective Communication
- Barrier Removal
- Reasonable Accommodations
- Rehabilitation Act of 1973
- Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM)
- Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC)
- ADA Compliance Requirements

## Core ADA Law & Regulations

- [The Americans with Disabilities Act](https://www.ada.gov): Homepage for ADA civil rights law covering disability access nationwide
- [Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, As Amended](https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada): Full text of ADA statute including 2008 Amendments Act
- [Law, Regulations & Standards](https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs): DOJ regulations explaining disability rights and ADA obligations
- [Americans with Disabilities Act Title II Regulations](https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/regulations/title-ii-2010-regulations): Title II regulations for state/local government accessibility

## Web & Digital Accessibility

- [Notice of Proposed Rulemaking on Web Accessibility](https://www.ada.gov/resources/2023-07-20-web-nprm): NPRM fact sheet on Title II web/mobile accessibility standards for govt
- [State and Local Governments: First Steps for Web Compliance](https://www.ada.gov/resources/web-rule-first-steps): Implementation guide for state/local govt Title II web compliance
- [Accessibility of State and Local Government Websites](https://www.ada.gov/resources/accessibility-govt-websites): Guidance on making state/local government websites accessible

## Title III: Public Accommodations & Businesses

- [Businesses That Are Open to the Public](https://www.ada.gov/topics/title-iii): Title III overview for public accommodations and business compliance
- [ADA Title III Technical Assistance Manual](https://www.ada.gov/resources/title-iii-manual): Technical manual for Title III public accommodations compliance
- [ADA Update: A Primer for Small Business](https://www.ada.gov/resources/title-iii-primer): Small business guide to Title III compliance and accessible design

## Key Topics & Issue Areas

- [Topics](https://www.ada.gov/topics): Topic overviews covering key ADA areas like service animals and parking
- [Frequently Asked Questions about Service Animals](https://www.ada.gov/resources/service-animals-faqs): FAQ on service animal requirements and public accommodation rules
- [Mobility Devices](https://www.ada.gov/topics/mobility-devices): Rights for wheelchair and power-driven mobility device users
- [Telehealth](https://www.ada.gov/topics/telehealth): Healthcare provider obligations for accessible telehealth services
- [Rights of Parents with Disabilities](https://www.ada.gov/topics/parental-rights): Child welfare agency obligations for parents with disabilities

## Compliance & Technical Guidance

- [ADA Requirements: Testing Accommodations](https://www.ada.gov/resources/testing-accommodations): Technical assistance on testing accommodations for standardized exams
- [ADA Compliance Brief: Restriping Parking Spaces](https://www.ada.gov/resources/restriping-parking-spaces): Requirements for accessible parking when restriping facilities
- [Protecting Voter Rights with Disabilities](https://www.ada.gov/resources/protecting-voter-rights): Guidance on ADA and federal voting accessibility requirements

## Filing Complaints & Support

- [File a Complaint](https://www.ada.gov/file-a-complaint): Steps to file ADA discrimination complaint with federal agencies
- [Questions and Answers: The ADA and Hiring Police Officers](https://www.ada.gov/resources/ada-and-hiring-officers-qa): Q&A on ADA employment rights for police department hiring
